original.target_description: Problem 11: choice of risky Plan N under specific save-$250,000 goal versus do-your-best goal, matching the described comparison on PDF p. 16 (printed p. 94).

n.location: PDF p. 16; printed p. 94, Problem 11 response lines
n.quote:
Which plan will you choose? [Do your best, N ⫽ 65]           Plan N (24%)
        Which plan will you choose? [Save $250,000, N ⫽ 66] Plan N (47%)
n.sample_role: Participants/respondents in the two mutually exclusive goal-condition groups of the Problem 11 comparison: do your best (65) and save $250,000 (66).
n.exclusions: No exclusions or missing responses stated for the printed problem-specific counts.

es.location: PDF p. 16; printed p. 94, Problem 11 results
es.quote:
The number of people who choose the more risky Plan N doubles when
people have a specific rather than a ‘‘do your best’’ goal (p ⬍ .01 by χ 2 ).

notes: Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders; no extraction attempted for them. Primary source identity verified. Analytic N sum: 65 participants in the do-your-best group + 66 participants in the specific-goal group = 131 participants in the two-condition comparison; distinct condition counts, not whole-paper recruitment or N inferred from df. Chi-square is named but its numeric statistic is not printed. Same comparison reports p < .01, retained here only as context because pval_value_o is unassigned; the p field is a placeholder. No statistic computed from rounded percentages.
